mechanism: Treat the scalar face H = C − 2E as a single stochastic integral against the compensated prime measure dΠ = Σ_p δ_p − dt/log t: the kernel-checked reindexing E(x) = Σ_d M(d)·Π(I_d(x)) over the disjoint reciprocal intervals I_d(x) = (max(y,⌊x/(d+1)⌋), ⌊x/d⌋] is, in renewal/point-process language, a martingale transform of the compensated prime arrival process with predictable weights M(d); the claim is that C's zero-mode-centered, PNT-corrected comb mass collapses (by exact partial summation, provable and Lean-checkable) into the same transform, so that H(x) = Σ_d w_d(x)·Π(I_d(x)) + O(x^{1/2}·polylog) for one explicit signed weight family w_d built from M(d) — an exact transformation preserving the C − 2E correlation, replacing value-level statistical correlation by kernel-level algebraic compensation. Then bound the transform in L² rather than L¹: its predictable quadratic variation is QV(x) = Σ_d w_d(x)²·E|Π(I_d)|² ≈ Σ_d M(d)²·(x/d²)/log x, which under the inductive hypothesis M(d) ≪ d^{1/2+ε} for d ≤ √x is ≪ x^{1+ε} — i.e., the same strong induction that provably diverges in L¹ (obstacle 4: Σ_d d^{1/2}·x/d² ≍ x, too large) closes at exactly rung 2 in mean square. Deterministically, the model orthogonality E[Π(I_d)Π(I_{d'})] = 0 must be replaced by two named estimates over the internal d-family at the pinned sample x = X_n: (i) the Reciprocal Variance bound V(x) = Σ_{d≤√x} M(d)²·Π(I_d(x))² ≪_ε x^{1+ε}, a Montgomery–Soundararajan/Goldston–Montgomery-type variance for primes in the reciprocal partition of [√x, x]; and (ii) the Reciprocal Dispersion Estimate (RDE) Σ_{d≠d'} M(d)M(d')·Π(I_d(x))·Π(I_{d'}(x)) ≪_ε x^{1+ε}, a pair-correlation statement for primes in disjoint short intervals. Because the samples are the complete squares X_n = (n+1)²−1, the induction from scale √x to x has depth log₂log₂ x, so a fixed multiplicative constant loss per level compounds only to (log x)^{O(1)}, absorbable into x^ε — the induction skeleton genuinely closes if (i) and (ii) hold with polylog losses. The window/Gram form is then handled for free: the Gram value equals the window energy of the high path (kernel-verified identity in CanonicalGapAncestryQuadraticClosure.lean), and a pointwise bound |H(X_{N+r})| ≪ (N+r)^{1+ε} summed over r < H ≤ N gives C·H·N^{2+2ε} directly.
new_leverage: Three things a standard application would not give. First, the compensated-process formulation converts the empirically observed C ≈ 2E correlation from a statistical fact about values into a candidate algebraic identity about kernels — the compensator (Li term) is subtracted inside a single Stieltjes integral, so no triangle inequality ever separates C from E; this is precisely the "exact transformation preserving the C − 2E correlation" the route doc asks for, and it is canonical renewal-theory machinery (compensated counting process), not an import. Second, the L¹→L² shift resolves obstacle 4's stated failure quantitatively: the identical inductive input |M(d)| ≤ Kd^{1/2+ε} that produces a divergent operator with absolute values (Σ d^{1/2}·x/d² ≍ x) produces a convergent quadratic variation (Σ d^{1+2ε}·x/d² ≪ x^{1+ε}) — the failure was an artifact of the norm, not the induction. Third, the square-sample synchronization makes the induction depth log log x, so the usual killer of strong inductions (constant blowup per level) costs only polylog; and the reduction transfers the rung-2 difficulty off the Möbius/parity axis entirely, onto prime pair-correlation statements (Montgomery-type), which are a genuinely different conjectural axis: pair correlation neither implies nor is implied by RH in known implications, so this is a real reduction, not a restatement.
target_estimate: Named estimate I would prove (the deliverable is a chain of three, in decreasing certainty). (1) Kernel-Collapse Identity: for pinned x = X_n in a synchronized block (L_k, U_k], C(x) − 2E(x) = Σ_{d=1}^{D(x)} w_d(x)·Π(I_d(x)) + R(x) with |R(x)| ≪ x^{1/2}(log x)^2, where w_d is an explicit signed weight with w_d ≪ |M(d)| + d^{1/2}, Π(I) the compensated prime count on I, D(x) ≍ √x — exact, no averaging, formalizable. (2) Rung-0 bound CRK-0: |C(x) − 2E(x)| ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/4}) uniformly over pinned block samples, by splitting at D₀ = exp((log x)^{1/2}): Vinogradov–Korobov endpoint discrepancies (x/d)exp(−c(log x)^{3/5}) for d ≤ D₀, and the classical M(d) ≪ d·exp(−c√(log d)) against trivial interval bounds x/d² for d > D₀. (3) Conditional closure theorem: [Reciprocal Variance: Σ_{d≤√x} M(d)²Π(I_d(x))² ≪_ε x^{1+ε} at every pinned X_n] AND [RDE: Σ_{d≠d'≤√x} M(d)M(d')Π(I_d(x))Π(I_{d'}(x)) ≪_ε x^{1+ε}] together imply ProjectedRenewalQuadraticBoundedStatement(Λ) for the required Λ, via the log log-depth induction with per-level constant loss A and total loss (log x)^{log₂A}. Losses throughout: polylog in (1) and (3); the ε in (3) doubles per induction level but only log log x levels occur.

obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: The identity (1) and the induction skeleton (3) are exact and fully pinned at x = X_n; no averaging over the start ever occurs, so W_{k-1} cannot land in an exceptional set of starts. The conjectural inputs are stated pinned, but their internal structure averages over the index d at fixed x: the reciprocal partition supplies ~√x disjoint intervals as an internal family, and the L² formulation tolerates exceptional d's whose total contribution is ≪ x^{1+ε} — exceptional-set tolerance is moved from the forbidden start variable to the harmless interval-index variable. Honest residual: known techniques prove such variance bounds only averaged over x as well; removing that x-average is the hard analytic core and I do not claim it is done.
obstacle_positions.large_sieve_non_transfer: Conceded in full against large-sieve routes: no map from off-diagonal pairs to a shared modulus is constructed. The angle routes around the obstacle rather than through it — the missing modulus family is replaced by the internal d-family of disjoint reciprocal intervals, and off-diagonal control is requested as prime pair-correlation between disjoint short intervals (RDE), which needs no shared-modulus multiplicity accounting at all.
obstacle_positions.not_bombieri_vinogradov: Agreed and embraced: the inputs I request are exactly signed short-interval/dispersion estimates over the disjoint ordinary intervals of the reciprocal family — the mechanism class the source route doc itself names as plausible — with no residue classes to varying moduli anywhere.
obstacle_positions.strong_induction_failure: This is the angle's central engagement. The declared failure inserts |M(d)| ≤ Kd^{1/2+ε} with absolute values, giving Σ_d d^{1/2}·(x/d²) ≍ x — an L¹ operator that cannot close. The compensated transform runs the same inductive input through quadratic variation: Σ_d M(d)²·(x/d²) ≪ x^{1+ε}, which closes at rung 2. The failure was a property of the norm, not the induction; square sampling caps the induction depth at log log x so constants survive.
obstacle_positions.parity: The reduction's terminal conjectural objects are prime pair-correlation and prime short-interval variance statements — not μ-weighted sieve outputs — so sieve parity has no direct jurisdiction over them; μ enters only through the inductively-known weights M(d), which are data, not sieved quantities. Parity could resurface if proving RDE itself demands bilinear μ information; position on that is unestablished and flagged. The transfer to the prime-correlation axis is a deliberate parity dodge, not a parity refutation.
obstacle_positions.finite_range_deception: Numerics are used strictly as falsifiers, never as support: the kill test computes exact per-d decompositions and empirical exponents only to destroy the angle, and no exponent or correlation observed over finite ranges is cited as evidence for any rung. The rung-2 claim rests entirely on the conditional theorem (3), whose hypotheses are named conjectures, not fitted exponents.

kill_test: An afternoon of symbolic partial summation plus exact computation at pinned samples X_n in blocks k = 3,4 (x up to ~10^7). Kill 1 (cheapest, decisive): carry out the partial-summation collapse of C − 2E and check for a deterministic drift term — if centering leaves a non-martingale drift of size ≫ x^{1/2}·polylog (e.g., an uncancelled Li-difference mass ≍ x/log x), the Kernel-Collapse Identity is false and the entire L² program never starts; this is checkable symbolically and numerically (residual R(x) growing like x^{θ} with θ > 0.6 across the sampled range kills it). Kill 2: compute the per-d cancellation ratio ρ(x) = Σ_d |C_d − 2E_d| / Σ_d (|C_d| + 2|E_d|); if ρ(x) ≈ 1 throughout (cancellation lives only across d, tied statistically to the values of M(d)), the compensation is statistical rather than algebraic and the kernel-level claim dies. Kill 3: compute the diagonal Σ_d M(d)²Π(I_d)² and off-diagonal dispersion sums exactly; empirical exponent clearly above ~1.2 in x over these ranges kills the L² closure hypotheses as stated (subject to obstacle 6: survival proves nothing, only failure is informative).
rung0_plan: Same machinery, degraded norms. Use the transform identity (or, at this rung, even the raw triangle inequality on the reindexed family — rung 0 does not need the compensation). Split at D₀ = exp((log x)^{1/2}). Head d ≤ D₀: each Π(I_d) is a difference of two endpoint discrepancies each ≪ (x/d)·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5}) by Vinogradov–Korobov; with |M(d)| ≤ d the head is ≪ x·D₀·exp(−c(log x)^{3/5}) = x·exp((log x)^{1/2} − c(log x)^{3/5}) = o(x). Tail d > D₀: bound |Π(I_d)| trivially by ≪ x/d² + 1 and use the classical M(d) ≪ d·exp(−c√(log d)): the tail is ≪ x·log x·exp(−c(log D₀)^{1/2}) = x·log x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/4}) = o(x). Total: |C − 2E| ≪ x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/4}), pinned, uniform over synchronized blocks — PNT-strength with a classical exponential saving, purely from zero-free-region inputs. This confirms the machinery closes at rung 0 with graceful degradation: the identical d-split and the identical weight bounds, with L¹ norms where rung 2 needs L².
plausible_partial: Realistically provable at bounded effort: (a) the Kernel-Collapse Identity (1) with explicit w_d and R(x) ≪ x^{1/2}(log x)^2 — finite exact algebra plus partial summation, plausibly Lean-formalizable against the existing kernel-checked reindexing; (b) the rung-0 bound CRK-0 with the exp(−c(log x)^{1/4}) saving, fully unconditional and pinned; (c) the conditional closure theorem (3) — [pinned reciprocal variance + RDE] implies the target statement — including the log log-depth constant bookkeeping; this is a genuine RH-equivalent-to-prime-pair-correlation transfer theorem in these exact coordinates and is the most valuable deliverable; (d) the kill-test computations documented. NOT plausibly provable at bounded effort: any unconditional rung 1 — power savings pointwise in the reciprocal short intervals sit at zero-density/density-hypothesis depth, and I can defend no unconditional θ < 1 from this lens; the honest unconditional ceiling of the angle today is rung 0 with exponential-log savings.
self_assessed_risk: The assumption most likely to be false is the Kernel-Collapse Identity: that C's zero-mode-centered all-plus comb mass collapses, by exact algebra, into the same Mertens-weighted compensated transform as 2E with only an O(x^{1/2}·polylog) residual. If the centering instead leaves a drift term of intermediate size (between x^{1/2} and x) that the observed C ≈ 2E correlation is statistically absorbing, then the compensation is value-level, not kernel-level, the martingale-transform structure evaporates, and everything above rung 0 collapses back onto the raw dispersion problem. Secondary risk, stated plainly: the pinned reciprocal variance hypothesis may be circular — a pinned x^{1+ε} variance for primes over the reciprocal partition could secretly be RH-hard in the same way the original target is (pinned pointwise statements usually are), in which case the 'transfer to the pair-correlation axis' is a relabeling rather than a reduction, and the conditional theorem (c), while true, would carry no strategic value.
